Tests generated from real user sessions found faults as well as or better than white-box suites, and found different faults (Elbaum et al., TSE 2005).

Commercial tools that turn traffic into tests (Meticulous, Checksum) are web-only and run in Chrome with stubbed network. Meticulous replays recorded responses rather than exercising the backend. No independent measured results were found for them.
Maestro marks `assertWithAI` experimental and non-blocking by default (`optional: true`) because of unstable AI responses.

Vision-LLM oracles show research gains: Trident's precision rose 108–147% over the baselines. Their answers are unstable across repeated queries, as MT-GUI's flakiness baseline shows. Applitools' "99.9999%" figure comes with no methodology.
publishers: arxiv; icse 2026 journal-first per search listing

text: LLMs can recover state machines from source code with more than 90% precision in the protocol domain (ProtocolGPT). XState provides deterministic path enumeration. No published system was found that has an LLM build an XState model of a UI app and then enumerate test paths.
Detox's official support window is RN 0.77–0.84; RN 0.72 is outside it and only "best effort".
RN 0.72 support was added in Detox 20.17.0 (confirms Worker A1).

Detox has explicit iOS 26 work: maintainer-run iOS 26 suite (most tests passed), "iOS 26 compatibility" in 20.47.0, further iOS 26 fixes through 20.51.x. So current Detox + Xcode 26 is maintained; _older_ Detox (pre-20.47) on iOS 26 is not shown to work.
No evidence found either way that Detox ≥20.47 builds/runs against RN 0.72.17; the iOS-26-capable Detox and the RN-0.72-supported Detox may not overlap.

Detox's flake advantage depends on the app idling; endless timers/animations/polling/websockets cause wait-for-idle timeouts, and the fixes (URL blacklist, disabling sync) forfeit part of that advantage. Whether Firebase listeners on this app keep it busy is unverified.
Maestro #1585 is **closed** (2026-03-09, not fixed, closed for lack of repro) — Worker/brief statement "open since 2023" is outdated.

An open, specific Maestro bug (#3538) on Xcode 26.3–26.6 / iOS 26.2–26.5, reported on 2.8.0–2.11.0, describes the driver dying mid-suite and all later flows failing — consistent with the local crash pattern.
Maestro maintainers say an iOS driver rework is in progress that should remove this failure class; no shipped rework appears in CHANGELOG through 2.11.0 (2026-09-29).

Running a whole folder in one `maestro test` session does **not** avoid the #3538 failure; one driver death fails every remaining flow in that suite. Per-flow invocations isolate failures but pay driver startup each time (where the local crashes happen).

`maestro mcp` has open iOS session-handling bugs relevant to an agent loop: stale driver after simulator erase/reboot (reported on Xcode 26.6/iOS 26.5) and a shared driver port across simulators. Workaround: one MCP process per simulator session, restart after erase.
Maestro MCP gives an agent `inspect_screen` (hierarchy JSON) + inline-YAML `run`, a direct authoring loop; Detox has no equivalent MCP-style exploration tool found.

Wix Pilot (Detox Copilot successor) exists and drives tests from natural-language steps through LLMs at runtime; the README does not describe generating durable Detox code, so it is not a code generator for a CI suite.
Published flakiness numbers (Detox <2%, Maestro <1%) come from Maestro's own marketing with no methodology; no independent quantitative comparison was found.
Expo documents only Maestro for EAS Workflows E2E, a non-vendor ecosystem signal toward Maestro for the generic case.
No source evaluates how well LLMs write Detox TS vs Maestro YAML.

Firebase's own MCP server ships a prompt that scans a codebase for Firestore paths, generates rules plus a `@firebase/rules-unit-testing` suite, runs it on the emulator, and stops to report on rule failures instead of editing rules. This is direct prior art for LLM-generated rules tests from code.
In LocAgent, removing graph traversal lowered function-level localization accuracy (ablation), so structure gave a measurable comprehension-adjacent gain in that setting.
Async Wait accounted for 32.5% of the 83 flaky mobile UI tests in Romano et al. (whether it is the largest mobile category was not verified in the text).

StrykerJS's generic command test runner can drive any test command (e.g. a device E2E runner) by exit code, but runs the full suite for every mutant, so exhaustive mutation of a device E2E suite is impractical.
